knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The barrier and warning signs are set out before any glass is wet, so that people are kept away from the work. A chair under the window is an unstable access method and is ruled out by the stop-work rule.
Glazing that can only be reached by ladder is outside the ground-level method. The learner stops, does not climb, and reports it. The lesson does not grant training or a licence for this work.
Overlapping figure-of-eight passes, with the blade wiped after each pass, remove the solution without leaving smears. Scrubbing until the solution dries, or one straight pass, leaves marks.

practicalCriteria: Given a supplied ground-level window and the barrier and signs, the learner sets out the barrier and signs before any glass is wet, observed by the assessor.
The learner puts on gloves and goggles, and washes and checks a supplied bucket, cloth, ferret and blade, confirming no two products are mixed, observed by the assessor.

The learner applies the supplied diluted solution with a ferret or dolly, allows contact time, and removes it with overlapping figure-of-eight passes, wiping the blade after each pass. Pass condition: the assessor finds no smear or run on the test pane when it is checked in good light.

Given a supplied scenario of a window that needs a ladder to reach, the learner states the stop-work rule, does not climb, and describes the report they would make. Pass condition: the learner stops and reports without prompting.
The learner washes, dries, colour-codes and stores the supplied equipment, keeping clean and dirty equipment apart, observed by the assessor.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record for each practical criterion
Photo of the test pane after the learner's work, checked in good light
Scope check or stop-work report for the supplied scenario
stopWorkCriteria: Learner climbs a ladder, or stands on furniture, a box or a step, to reach glass
Learner mixes two products, or uses a product with no label displayed
Learner works without eye protection while a solution is in use
Learner works with the barrier and warning signs not set out, and a member of the public is in or near the work area
Learner uses a dirty cloth or blade on the final pass, or leaves a solution to dry on the glass
Learner undertakes any height work without the required training or licence, which this assessment does not confer
